promises.quote: Introducing library conditions within the dispensary. Commencing with immediate effect.
promises.summary: Introduce library conditions in dispensary to reduce noise and distractions.

promises.quote: the exit route (after 5pm) from the 31st January department which is currently located next to the 2020 accuracy checking area. Staff will exit the department via the pharmacy reception exit, preventing staff using the dispensary as a thoroughfare
promises.summary: Change exit route after 5pm to prevent staff using dispensary as thoroughfare.

promises.quote: Reviewing the layout of the dispensary with the aim 29th February of separating the areas used for different parts of 2020 the dispensing process and improving the flow of work.
promises.summary: Review dispensary layout to separate dispensing areas and improve workflow.

promises.quote: closed loop dispensing" (linking the 30th June 2020 electronic prescribing system to the pharmacy dispensing system and robot) with the aim of reducing dispensing errors and improving efficiency and therefore reducing the number of staff needed in the dispensary
promises.summary: Implement closed loop dispensing linking electronic systems to reduce errors.

promises.quote: Updating the accuracy checking procedure which 31st December will incorporate a second check for all intravenous 2019 fluids.
promises.summary: Update accuracy checking procedure to include second check for IV fluids.

concerns.quote: one of the root causes for the medication error, was the Phosphate Polyfusor product design
Product design on the Polyfusors in question

Healthcare Professional should check the name of the medication on the prescription chart against the name of the medication on the packaging and labelling of the medication at the time of each administration of medication to ensure that the correct medication is always administered to a patient
concerns.hazard: failure to verify medication name before administration

concerns.quote: system of checking medications against the packaging, labelling and prescription chart at the time of receipt by the ward. Furthermore, to consider documentary evidence of the fact that the medication packaging has been checked against the prescription chart and an acknowledgement of receipt of the correct medication by the pharmacy and ward staff, evidenced by a signature of the recipient
Training, Auditing, Supervision and monitoring of all staff, particularly Nursing and Pharmacy staff, in relation to the above issues
concerns.hazard: insufficient staff competency monitoring for medication verification

promises.quote: The MHRA considers that the only reliable way for unambiguous identification of a particular medicine is via the information printed on the package labelling.
promises.summary: MHRA emphasizes label as primary identifier to avoid medication errors

concerns.quote: That the visual similarity of tablets of differing strengths of carbimazole to each other and to aspirin presents a risk of inadvertent overdose; and That the dispensing process in the community for carbimazole appears to contribute to rather than mitigating the risk

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that look‑alike medication packaging or labeling can lead to dispensing errors because staff rely on superficial cues rather than verifying the product against the prescription.
links.earlier_quote: Manufacturers are able to produce medication in almost identical boxes which is very likely to contribute to dispensing errors and potentially patient deaths.
links.later_quote: The Pharmacy and Nursing Matron [name redacted], concurred that the staff involved in the incident had relied on the word Polyfusor, without actually checking the medication packaging against the prescription chart and label.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that look‑alike medication appearance can cause dispensing errors. The earlier report focuses on nearly identical outer packaging, while the later report concerns tablet shape and strength similarity to aspirin.
